name: ceiling_guard_dormancy_nat_vent_active_in_band__hvac_fan
description: [hvac_fan twin of golden 'ceiling_guard_dormancy_nat_vent_active_in_band'; Issue #1193] ODE ceiling guard stays dormant when nat-vent is active AND indoor is within comfort band. Outdoor cooler than indoor provides free cooling — no HVAC escalation needed.
source: Issue #1193: hvac_fan twin of golden 'ceiling_guard_dormancy_nat_vent_active_in_band' (pre-#1140 version, fan configured). The golden is locked and now asserts the no-fan 'paused' result.

verdict.summary: [hvac_fan twin] Ceiling guard correctly defers to nat-vent when outdoor is cooler than indoor and indoor is within the comfort band
verdict.observed_behavior: nat_vent_active=True with indoor 73F within band [70F, 74F], outdoor 65F — ceiling guard bypassed
verdict.expected_behavior: ceiling guard dormant (bypassed), nat-vent continues, no HVAC intervention

events.note: Morning: indoor 73F within comfort band [70F, 74F], outdoor 65F (8F cooler than indoor — nat-vent favorable)
Window opens: outdoor 65F < indoor 73F, indoor > comfort_heat 70F, outdoor < threshold 77F — nat-vent activates
Same-instant refresh so the (zero-debounce) sensor timer fires: the harness only advances its virtual clock on event boundaries.

30 min later: indoor still 73F (within band), outdoor still 65F. Nat-vent providing free cooling. Ceiling guard should remain dormant — ODE branch is bypassed entirely when nat-vent is active. A predicted_indoor curve that crosses comfort_cool (74F) within the lead time is supplied so the ceiling guard has a breach to act on: without the dormancy rule it would escalate.

assertions.reason: [hvac_fan twin] sensor_open: outdoor 65F < indoor 73F, indoor > comfort_heat 70F, outdoor 65F <= threshold 77F — nat-vent activates

[hvac_fan twin] temp_update with nat-vent active and indoor 73F within band [70F, 74F], outdoor 65F < indoor: no exit condition fires (indoor > comfort_heat, outdoor < indoor, outdoor < threshold). Ceiling guard is bypassed by simulator routing when nat_vent_active=True. Nat-vent continues as expected.

notes: hvac_fan twin (Issue #1193): with the HVAC fan configured, an open window with usable outdoor air is ventilation (fan on), not a pause. This scenario pins the ventilation/exit/setback decision only; it deliberately does NOT assert the cool setpoint that production also arms during hvac_fan ventilation (nat_vent_ac_assist_armed), which is the rule-3 question tracked in #1142.

Issue #1193 revert-proofing: a thermal_model (confidence high) and a predicted_indoor curve that crosses comfort_cool within the lead time are supplied so the ODE ceiling guard is actually evaluated here; without them the guard returns MODEL_INELIGIBLE/NOT_APPLICABLE and a dormant-guard assertion passes vacuously. With the dormancy rule removed the guard escalates (clears nat-vent, commands cool) and the nat-vent assertion fails.
